title: Smallness of relative simplex-extension homotopy classes
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Use quasicategories, simplicial products, mapping spaces and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $C$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory, $n\geq1$, and $b:\partial\Delta^n\to C$ a simplicial map, where $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of all proper faces of $\Delta^n$. Write $x=b(0)$ and $y=b(n)$. Assume only that $\operatorname{Map}_C(x,y)$ is equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small space. Let $E_b$ be the set of extensions $f:\Delta^n\to C$ with $f|_{\partial\Delta^n}=b$. On $E_b$ take the equivalence relation generated by pairs $f,g$ admitting a simplicial map $H:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ with endpoints $f,g$ and restriction $b\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$. Then $E_b/{\sim}$ is in bijection with a $\mathcal U$-small set. In particular, the assertion includes $E_b=\varnothing$. No bound is assumed on the number of actual simplices of $C$ or on its other mapping spaces.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.1.1 and the relative-extension counting argument in Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2), p. 419 (PDF p. 436). This isolates the fixed-boundary assertion used in that induction, using a small model of the single endpoint mapping space. Read online; no local HTT copy is present in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: If $E_b$ is empty, its quotient is empty and is in bijection with the empty set in $\mathcal U$. Henceforth suppose it is nonempty. Set $M=\operatorname{Map}_C(x,y)$; it is a Kan complex by the enhanced functor calculus, and by hypothesis it is equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex. Because $n\geq1$, every vertex of $\Delta^n$ belongs to its boundary; thus all the vertex tracks of every homotopy in the question are constant identity edges. In particular there is no additional invertibility restriction on these relative homotopies.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.1.1 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2), printed p.419; expanded via a small Kan model rather than a homotopy-group cardinal estimate.

proof.text: Let $A=R\mathfrak C[C]$ be the object-preserving locally Kan replacement supplied by coherent-nerve comparison, and put $C'=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$. All of this is formed in $\mathcal U'$, without making a smallness assertion there relative to $\mathcal U$. The adjunction unit followed by replacement gives $u:C\to C'$. Every simplicial set is cofibrant in the Joyal structure; since the coherent-nerve adjunction is a Quillen equivalence, its derived unit at $C$ is an equivalence, and the derived-adjunction computation identifies that unit with the displayed map. Passing to homotopy categories gives an ordinary localization at the model weak equivalences: testing the coherent-localization universal property against nerves of ordinary categories gives exactly the ordinary universal property for inverting those maps. Thus the displayed unit becomes an isomorphism in that ordinary localization. Detection of weak equivalences in a model localization therefore says that $u$ is a categorical equivalence. In particular $C'$ is a quasicategory. Apply case (ii) of relative homotopy invariance with $(B,A)=(\Delta^n,\partial\Delta^n)$ and boundary $b$: it gives a bijection from the quotient in the question to the relative extension classes for $ub$ in $C'$. The all-vertices hypothesis was checked in step 1.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.1.1 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2), printed p.419; expanded via a small Kan model rather than a homotopy-group cardinal estimate.

proof.text: Put $m=n-1$ and $T=A(u(x),u(y))$, using the identification of the object sets of $\mathfrak C[C]$ and its replacement; thus the objects here are the original vertices $x,y$. The cube comparison applied to the boundary $ub$ supplies a fixed map $a:\partial Q_m\to T$ and identifies its relative simplex-extension classes with $[Q_m,T]_a$. Explicitly the coordinates record the intermediate vertices of the long-arrow subset poset, the zero faces come from omission of an intermediate vertex, and the one faces come from splitting the long arrow and composing. Thus all the other mapping data of the boundary remain fixed, rather than being varied during the cube comparison. When $n=1$, this is the point $Q_0$ with empty boundary, so it gives precisely the component classes of arrows.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.1.1 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2), printed p.419; expanded via a small Kan model rather than a homotopy-group cardinal estimate.

proof.text:
The endpoint mapping complex $T$ is equivalent to $M$ without any hypothesis on the other mapping spaces of $C$. Indeed write $V=\mathfrak C[C](x,y)$ and use the natural zigzag
$$T\ \xleftarrow{\sim}\ V\ \xleftarrow{\theta}\ |M|_Q\ \xrightarrow{p_M}\ M.$$
The first map is the local weak equivalence of the replacement $\mathfrak C[C]\to A$; the other two weak equivalences are exactly the pinched-resolution comparison and its natural map $p$. Choose a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex $K$ equivalent to $M$, as the hypothesis permits. Consequently $T$ and $K$ are isomorphic in an ordinary localization of the Kan model category in $\mathcal U'$. The Kan model-structure statement makes every simplicial set cofibrant, since its initial map is degreewise injective, and makes both $T$ and $K$ fibrant, since both are Kan complexes. The mapping-class lemma realizes an isomorphism $\gamma T\to\gamma K$ by an actual map $v:T\to K$, and the localization-detection lemma makes $v$ a weak homotopy equivalence. This step chooses a map representing an equivalence, not an actual small presentation of all the simplices of $T$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.1.1 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2), printed p.419; expanded via a small Kan model rather than a homotopy-group cardinal estimate.

proof.text: Apply case (i) of relative homotopy invariance to $v:T\to K$ and $\partial Q_m\subseteq Q_m$. It gives a bijection $[Q_m,T]_a\cong[Q_m,K]_{va}$ by postcomposition. There is no demand that the old boundary lift through a map out of $K$: the new boundary is exactly $va$. Case (i) permits arbitrary simplicial subsets, so it also applies when $m=0$ and the boundary is empty.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.1.1 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, proof of (1) implies (2), printed p.419; expanded via a small Kan model rather than a homotopy-group cardinal estimate.

proof.text: The simplicial sets $Q_m$ and $K$ are $\mathcal U$-small. A simplicial map between them is an element of the small product $\prod_{d\geq0}\operatorname{Set}((Q_m)_d,K_d)$ satisfying the simplicial equations, so the set of all such maps belongs to $\mathcal U$. Requiring the boundary to be $va$ defines a subset of this small set. Homotopies are likewise maps between small simplicial sets; alternatively the equivalence relation they generate is a subset of the square of the small extension set. Its quotient therefore belongs to $\mathcal U$, by closure of a universe under products, subsets and quotients. Composing the bijections of steps 2, 3 and 5 identifies $E_b/{\sim}$ with this small quotient. This uses only the small model $K$ of the single endpoint mapping space; it places no bound on actual simplices or other mapping spaces of $C$.
